objective: Independently find required correctness, security, compatibility, and evidence-claim defects in the frozen v0.5 offline route checker and tests.
deliverable: Prioritized findings with decisive counterexamples, exact reviewed commit and bounded ACCEPT_WITH_CAVEATS or REVISE verdict.
read_scope: Repository AGENTS.md and applicable local skill instructions
Python 3.10/3.11 standard library and automatically cleaned temporary fixtures created by the reviewed tests
write_scope: Only newly created, automatically cleaned per-test temporary directories owned by the standard-library runtime-route tests; no repository, Git, live Skill, or pre-existing file writes

authoritative_facts: User approved development and requires critical work on Astra without automatic downgrade.
The checker validates declared record consistency, not identity authenticity, complete-run closure, or host execution.
The current spawn tool permits an Astra request but does not by itself attest effective execution identity.
accepted_upstream_results: Design repair review V5-D1@2 accepted with caveats. Root reports 35 targeted methods passed on each runtime; verify rather than trust.
user_constraints: No repository edits, Git writes, network, installs, external model CLI, public actions, or further delegation.
permissions: Read declared sources, invoke bounded Python -B tests/probes using only owned self-cleaning temporary scratch.
Run targeted runtime-route tests and read-only legacy package validators. Do not run materialization/full-suite Git-writing tests.
non_goals: No live registry or policy review yet; those are not implemented at the reviewed commit.
Do not require authentication or a persistent scheduler outside the accepted design.
Do not fix findings; root owns source edits.

acceptance_checks: Read tests before implementation and compare every material rule to the accepted spec.
Probe bypasses, malformed nesting/identities, selected/effective comparison, overrides/pins, fallback, cycles, coverage, concurrency and deterministic CLI behavior.
Identify decisive missing tests or unsupported claims; do not report synthetic data as observed model identity.
Return verdict with no acceptance if Critical or Required defects remain; disclose untested scope.
